headline: South Asia: Houthis inflict major losses on Yemeni forces
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Houthis inflict major losses on Yemeni forces.
- Africa: Sudan: UN Condemns Deadly Wave of Drone Strikes in War-Torn Sudan.
- India: Iran faces rising threat as Baloch rebels step up attacks amid regional war pressure.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Marine Corps creates first medium missile battalion.
- Military Times, just now: Marine Corps creates first medium missile battalion.
As the service's first medium missile battalion, the 1st Battalion, 10th Marine Regiment, will be equipped with NMESIS as a complement to its artillery.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Honourable finale - Vaz believes OJ membership perfectly timed to cap public service career.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Honourable finale - Vaz believes OJ membership perfectly timed to cap public service career.
Certain that he is in the twilight of his political career, Transport Minister Daryl Vaz said his appointment to the Order of Jamaica (OJ) was perfectly timed and a fitting way to cap his life in public service. “The stars have aligned for me, and I could not want or ask for any better in terms of my leaving public service on the highest note possible,” he told The Gleaner after receiving the honour at yesterday’s annual National Honours and Awards Investiture Ceremony, held on the lawns of King’s House in St Andrew, where 140 Jamaicans were recognised.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: MoBay mayor urges St James residents to uphold resilience post-Melissa.
WESTERN BUREAU: Ahead of the one-year anniversary of Hurricane Melissa’s devastating impact on western Jamaica, Montego Bay Mayor Richard Vernon is urging residents of St James to continually embody the resilience and determination that the parish displayed during and after the Category 5 hurricane’s October 28, 2025 passage. Vernon made the call on Monday while addressing St James’ National Heroes Day Civic and Awards Ceremony in Sam Sharpe Square, Montego Bay, held under this year’s theme ‘Resilient People with a Proud Heritage’.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- The Moscow Times, one day ago: Annexed Crimea Begins Lifting Fuel Rationing Measures After Months of Shortages.

Two people have been injured and a fire broke out at a logistics complex due to a Russian drone strike on Kyiv Oblast on 20 October.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Ukrainian drone forces strike rare Russian BREM-1 armoured vehicle in Zaporizhzhia Oblast – video.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Three killed and two injured in Russian attack on Kramatorsk.
Russian attack has targeted Kramatorsk, damaging three multi-story residential buildings and causing multiple civilian casualties.

- Dawn (Pakistan), NDTV - Top Stories, Al Jazeera - Middle East, South China Morning Post - China, Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: UK to deploy fighter jets to help protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks.
British fighter planes will be deployed to help Saudi Arabia defend itself against increasing attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels, the UK government announced on Tuesday. The defence ministry said the deployment formed part of “additional defensive military support” to Riyadh. “The UK will fly defensive counter air missions to support the protection of Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure against aerial attack, using RAF Typhoon fighter jets,” the Ministry of Defence (MoD) said in a statement.

Adviser to the National Command Authority (NCA) and former director general of the Strategic Plans Division (SPD) retired Lieutenant General Mazhar Jamil has warned of the “risky” outcome for South Asia and beyond of a “dangerous ideology” shaping the Indian military mindset. “Indian military thinking is being shaped by a dangerous ideology, which conflates mythology with national power.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Rubio says India made 'substantial progress' in diversifying oil purchases.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that India had made “substantial progress” in diversifying its energy supplies, including away from its key importer, Russia. “What India has expressed repeatedly is their desire to diversify their energy portfolio, which is a smart thing to do,” Rubio said on a visit to India’s economic capital, Mumbai.
India - bottom line: Iran faces rising threat as Baloch rebels step up attacks amid regional war pressure.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Iran faces rising threat as Baloch rebels step up attacks amid regional war pressure.
Iran is grappling with escalating security issues fueled by assaults from Baloch separatists and Sunni militants. The People's Fighters Front has ramped up its operations in Sistan and Baluchistan, resulting in a rising number of casualties. In response, Iranian authorities are mobilizing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to combat these threats.
- Times of India - Top Stories, NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Shah meets families of anti-drug activists killed in Punjab; targets AAP.
Amit Shah visited families of drug-related victims in Punjab, expressing condolences and discussing safety issues. He criticised the AAP government for its failure to tackle the drug menace effectively. Shah highlighted the dangers faced by those who oppose drug trafficking in the state. The recent murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota escalated political tensions in Punjab.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Minor girl dragged out of garba pandal, assaulted near Mumbai.
On Monday night, a 17-year-old girl participated in a garba event in Santoshbhuvan. An 18-year-old youth, who was her friend, assaulted her after she stopped talking to him. The accused dragged her out of the garba pandal and attacked her. After the incident, Pelhar police registered a case against the accused under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The police promptly arrested him following the event.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: PM Modi invokes 'Ram Rajya' on Dussehra, warns against people hurting India's image.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the Dussehra celebrations and highlighted the importance of public welfare. He emphasized the need for social justice and self-reliance as central to national development. Modi reminded attendees of the ideals of Lord Ram, focusing on justice and equal opportunities. He encouraged recognizing India's potential while serving the poor and marginalized. The Prime Minister referenced Vijayadashami as a celebration of the triumph of good over evil.
